newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices see gains on low supplies.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices see gains on low supplies.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Tuesday rose on slow mill buying and dwindling supplies at the tail-end of the season, dealers said.
Reports that state-owned agencies hiked selling prices of cotton also aided buoyancy in the market.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees at 950/980 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 rose by 20 rupees at 1,990/2,030 rupees per maund.
"Daily average arrivals in the Punbaj region fell to 800/1,000 bales (170 kg each). Arrivals will drop further next month," one broker said.
"Gujarat varieties also looked up amid restricted supplies," he said.

In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 100/200 rupees at 14,200/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton rose by 200 rupees at 13,100 rupees per candy and kala-ginned rose by 100 rupees at 12,600 rupees per candy.

Dealers said state-owned Maharashtra Cotton Growers Federation have raised selling prices of cotton by 200/300 rupees per candy. They said other state-owned agencies may also hike prices due to the low supply situation.
